title: Perfora Oral Care (2026): Brush Specs, Head Costs and a 30-Day Routine
description: Official brush specifications and prices, an ADA-aligned safety checklist and the real annual cost of replacement heads. Peroxide percentages, AI coaching and the old subscriptions claim could not be verified.

forWho: Buyers comparing Perfora's battery, sonic and oscillating brushes on published specs and replacement-head cost rather than marketing badges.
People building a modest twice-daily routine who want a 30-day plan with clear stop rules for sensitivity.
skipIf: Anyone needing treatment for gum disease, persistent sensitivity or stained restorations — see a dentist; cosmetics and brushes are not a substitute for care.
Buyers relying on the earlier guide's 22% vs 35% peroxide comparison, 'AI coaching' claim or under-₹200/month subscription — none was verified.

content_blocks.heading: Which Perfora brush is worth buying, and what do replacement heads really cost?
content_blocks.body: The official electric-toothbrush collection listed the Smart Sonic at ₹2,999 (MRP ₹3,499), the pressure-sensor oscillating brush at ₹3,499 (MRP ₹3,999), the basic oscillating brush at ₹1,850 and the M001 battery brush at ₹1,199 on 26 Nov 2026. The Smart Sonic product page states 24,000–48,000 strokes/min, IPX7, roughly 60 days per charge, indicator bristles and a two-minute timer with 30-second area reminders. Using ADA's 3–4 month replacement guidance and a pack-of-two at ₹449, M001 rechargeable heads cost ₹898/year — about ₹74.83/month. The older peroxide percentages, AI coaching and subscription-price claims were not verified.

ctas.label: See the routine and head-cost model

items.title: Start simple: M001 battery brush at ₹1,199
items.body: The official collection lists Model 001 (battery operated) at ₹1,199 against ₹1,299 MRP, with two brush heads and two modes. It is the lowest-cost way to test whether an electric brush suits you. Replacement heads are listed at ₹449 for two, which drives the annualised cost model below.

items.title: Step up: Smart Sonic at ₹2,999
items.body: The Smart Sonic is listed at ₹2,999 (MRP ₹3,499) with a travel case, four brush heads and four modes. Its official page states 24,000–48,000 strokes/min, IPX7 waterproofing, roughly 60 days battery per charge, indicator bristles that signal replacement at about three months, and a two-minute timer with 30-second area reminders. We did not measure strokes, battery life or waterproofing.

items.title: Pressure control: oscillating brush at ₹3,499
items.body: The 'Pressure Sensor – Oscillating Electric Toothbrush' is listed at ₹3,499 (MRP ₹3,999) with three cleaning modes and a case. A pressure alert is useful because the ADA advises soft bristles and gentle pressure to reduce gingival injury. We did not verify the sensor's threshold or accuracy.

items.title: The 30-day routine, with stop rules
items.body: Days 1–3: brush twice for two minutes with the supplied soft brush, no whitening product. Days 4–7: add a water flosser at night if you already own one; the official homepage lists the Smart Dental Flosser at ₹2,799 (MRP ₹3,999). Days 8–14: introduce a whitening serum twice weekly, not daily, and stop if sensitivity appears. Days 15–30: continue the full routine. Persistent sensitivity, bleeding gums or pain means see a dentist, not add another product.

rows: 4 heads, 4 modes, travel case; page states 24,000–48,000 strokes/min, IPX7, ~60-day battery
Feature-rich starting point; strokes/min is a brand figure
Consider if you brush too hard; sensor not independently tested
Lowest entry cost for trying an electric brush
Cosmetic claim; peroxide percentage not verified
Optional step; learn the angle to avoid splashing

items.body: Choose on features you will use: timer and soft bristles first, pressure alert second, stroke count last. The ADA says both manual and powered brushes can remove plaque effectively.
Check the listed price and MRP on the exact variant. The collection showed several models from ₹949 to ₹3,499; colours and packs can differ.
Price the heads before the handle. Formula: heads per year = 12 ÷ months per head. At ADA's three-month interval that is four heads/year; a pack of two costing ₹449 means two packs, or ₹898/year.
Compare pack sizes. Oscillating heads were listed at ₹499 for two and Smart Sense heads at ₹649 for two; a cheaper handle can be dearer to maintain if its heads cost more.
Do not buy every whitening product at once. Start with a brush, add one adjunct after a week, and stop anything that causes sensitivity.
If an offer claims a subscription or guaranteed monthly price, verify the actual charge at checkout. The earlier 'under ₹200/month' figure was not confirmed on official pages.

items.label: Smart Sonic published specifications.
items.value: The official product page states 24,000–48,000 strokes/min, smart indicator bristles signalling replacement at roughly three months, IPX7 waterproofing, about 60 days of battery per charge and a two-minute timer with 30-second area reminders. These are brand-stated specifications, not Durza measurements.

items.label: Head packs are listed at ₹449–₹649 for two.
items.value: The official electric-toothbrush collection listed M001 rechargeable heads at ₹449 for two, oscillating heads at ₹499 for two and Smart Sense oscillating heads at ₹649 for two on 26 Nov 2026.

items.label: ADA: two minutes twice daily, soft bristles.
items.value: The American Dental Association's toothbrush guidance recommends brushing two minutes twice a day with a soft-bristled brush and gentle pressure, and states that both manual and powered brushes can be effective.

items.label: ADA: replace every three to four months.
items.value: The ADA recommends replacing toothbrushes approximately every three to four months, or sooner if bristles are matted or frayed. That is the basis of the head-cost model here.

items.label: Whitening percentages could not be verified.
items.value: The older guide compared 22% and 35% hydrogen peroxide and claimed potassium nitrate for sensitivity. We found official pages showing 'peroxide-free' on some products and enamel-safe/whitening claims on others, but no verified peroxide concentration for the serum, so no percentage is repeated.

items.label: ADA Seal status was not verified for Perfora.
items.value: The ADA explains that its Seal requires scientific evidence reviewed by the Council on Scientific Affairs. We did not confirm a Perfora listing, so no Seal is claimed; brand 'clinically proven' badges are treated as brand claims.

content_blocks.text: We checked official Perfora collection, product and homepage content and ADA toothbrush guidance on 26 Nov 2026. Prices and device specifications are attributed to Perfora; replacement-head costs are our arithmetic on the official pack prices and the ADA's three-to-four-month interval. Peroxide concentrations, AI coaching, subscription pricing and independent clinical results could not be verified and are not claimed. Durza earns a commission on qualifying purchases through tracked links at no extra cost to you.

items: Head-cost formula: 12 months ÷ 3 months per head = 4 heads/year; 4 ÷ 2 per pack = 2 packs; M001 rechargeable: 2 × ₹449 = ₹898/year ≈ ₹74.83/month.
Oscillating heads: 2 × ₹499 = ₹998/year ≈ ₹83.17/month. Smart Sense heads: 2 × ₹649 = ₹1,298/year ≈ ₹108.17/month. All are official listed pack prices, not subscription rates.
Sonic strokes per minute, battery days and IPX7 rating are brand-stated figures; Durza did not instrument a brush.
Whitening products are cosmetics. Do not ingest them, and stop use if sensitivity or irritation appears; consult a dentist for persistent symptoms.
The older 40,000 strokes/min vs 25,000 comparison, 22% vs 35% peroxide claim and 'AI coaching' description were not verified and are excluded.
Brush heads should not be shared, and bristles should be rinsed and air-dried after use, per ADA care guidance.

items.q: How is the Perfora smart brush better than a basic electric brush?
items.a: On the official page, the Smart Sonic adds four modes, a case, indicator bristles, a two-minute timer with 30-second area reminders, IPX7 and roughly 60 days of battery. We could not verify 'AI coaching' or a 40,000 vs 25,000 strokes/min comparison; the published range is 24,000–48,000 strokes/min.

items.q: What do replacement heads cost per month?
items.a: Using ADA's three-month replacement guidance: four heads a year, or two packs of two. At ₹449 per M001 rechargeable pack that is ₹898/year, about ₹74.83/month. At ₹499 for oscillating heads it is about ₹83.17/month. These are our calculations, not a subscription price.

The official page calls it enamel-safe, but we could not verify a peroxide concentration or independent clinical data. The older 22% vs 35% comparison is not repeated. Use as directed, do not ingest, and stop if you develop sensitivity.

items.q: How often should I change heads?
items.a: The ADA says every three to four months, or sooner if bristles are frayed. Perfora's indicator bristles are described as signalling replacement at about three months; that is a brand feature, not an independent measurement.

items.q: Did Durza test any Perfora product?
items.a: No. We compared published listings and ADA guidance on 26 Nov 2026. All costs and schedules are shown with inputs and assumptions.
